newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end 6.0 pct down on foreign sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end 6.0 pct down on foreign sales.

text.p: Battered Thai stock fell sharply by 6.0 percent at the close on Monday after sustained foreign selling of key banking and finance counters, brokers said.
The index finished down 60.26 points at 944.63, its lowest since August 3, 1993 when it ended at 938.24.
"Today's fall is one of the heaviest in the Thai bourse history when foreign firms joined hands and sold stocks," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance and Securities.

Although selling was seen across the board, the banking and finance sectors were the most badly bruised as foreign investors sold banks on a belief interest rates might not come down by year-end and would hurt their profits, brokers said.

Banks were also hit by last Friday's central bank measures to limit short-terms loans that offshore banking units would bring into Thailand for re-lending. Investors felt that could shrink profit-margins and sold, they added.
"Several foreign firms including Jardine Fleming Thanakom Securities and Credit Lyonnais continued to unload stocks in the market on concerns over Q3 earnings " Thanadech said.
Some research houses have forecast that banks' profit growth for 1996 will be amaller than last year's 15.6 percent and others see little prospects for rate cuts by year-end.
"The expected fall on the profit growth of banks this year along with plans by banks to raise deposit rates dampened the market sentiment," Thanadech said.
Bangkok Bank, Thailand's largest commercial bank, said on Friday that it was considering raising its deposit rates by about 25 basis points soon.
Key banks and some finance counters were among the the top 20 sold on the market and which posted heavy losses.
